items.title: We need to maintain a balance: Supreme Court refuses to lift ban on non-veg eateries near Gujarat Somnath Temple
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday refused to lift the ban on non-vegetarian eateries in the vicinity of Somnath Temple [ Taj Restaurant Owner Aakib Aminbhai Khan v. State of Gujarat & Ors. ]. A Bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale refused to interfere with an interim order passed by the Gujarat High Court that restored a ban on the preparation, sale and storage of non-vegetarian food around Somnath Temple. Responding to the argument by restaurant owners that the decision would kill of businesses and that 80 percent of the country eats meat, the Court said that a balance has to be maintained and it will not say anything at this stage. "We need to maintain a balance. We don’t say anything," the bench remarked. The Supreme Court nevertheless asked the High Court to give a final verdict in the matter as soon as possible. " We will request the High Court to expedite the hearing. It is the interim stage ," the Court observed. In a lighter vein, the Bench added, " Celebrate the festival of lights (Diwali) by having sweets. Leave veg or non-veg aside." Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale of Supreme Court The case concerns an August 10 notification issued by a District Magistrate in Gujarat. The notification imposed a prohibition on the preparation, sale and storage of non-vegetarian food at shops, restaurants, hotels and roadside stalls in specified areas. It covered seven specified stretches and areas, including all areas within 500 metres of Somnath Temple. Restaurant owners, who operate establishments in the region, challenged the notification before the Gujarat High Court.
